parts.text:
23 A cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO) is connected to a microphone which detects sound of constant
frequency.
The trace on the screen of the CRO is shown.
Which property of the sound wave is measured using only information from the CRO?
A
amplitude
B
period
C
speed
D
wavelength

hints: Notice the CRO trace is voltage against time: vertical deflection is microphone voltage and horizontal distance is set by the time-base control.
Connect one complete sine wave on the screen to one vibration of the sound: its time duration is the period $T$.
Ask what extra calibration each quantity needs: amplitude needs volts per division, while speed and wavelength need a distance in air.
walkthrough: Identify what the CRO displays: the microphone converts sound pressure to voltage, so the y-axis is voltage and the x-axis is time set by the time-base.
State the rule for period: the time for one complete oscillation is $T$, seen as the horizontal length of one full sine cycle from the same point on the wave to the next.
Check the trace: it shows about two full constant-frequency sine waves, so the cycle length in $\text{cm}$ times the time-base in $\text{s cm}^{-1}$ gives $T$ with no other apparatus.
Reject the others: amplitude needs the Y-gain calibration, and speed and wavelength need $v = f\lambda$ with a length measurement in the air, which the CRO does not provide.
Therefore only the period follows from the CRO settings alone. This is option B.

A.explanation: The vertical height gives voltage, but converting it to sound amplitude in $\text{Pa}$ needs the Y-gain in $\text{V cm}^{-1}$ and microphone response, not just the trace shape.

B.explanation: The horizontal length of one full sine cycle multiplied by the CRO time-base in $\text{s cm}^{-1}$ gives the period $T$ directly.

C.explanation: Wave speed needs $v = f\lambda$, so the CRO time trace alone without distance information cannot give speed.

D.explanation: Wavelength is a distance $\lambda$ in $\text{m}$, while the CRO x-axis shows time, so $\lambda$ cannot be found without wave speed.
